4 Integrated Course Lecture Frameworks (Original Slides + Structured Tables)

All 4 figures from your instructor's slides are directly embedded and linked into the concept map.

Column 1 Integration: Engagement & Motivation

  • Motivation (Less observable): The underlying reasons or forces for a given learning behaviour.
  • 3 Motivational Needs (SDT):
    • Autonomy: Feeling one has choice & willingly endorsing behavior ("You make your own decision / become more independent").
    • Competence: Experience of mastery and being effective in one's activity.
    • Relatedness: Need to feel connected and belongingness with others ("connect with others / social connection / connectivism").
  • Intrinsic vs. Extrinsic: Intrinsic ("from your perspective") vs. Extrinsic ("sth attracts you / earn money").
  • Engagement (More observable): Direct visible manifestation of motivation in Column 2.

Column 2 Integration: Representation of Students' Cognitive Engagement (Helme & Clarke, 2001)

Interaction Context 18 Observable Cognitive Indicators
1. Individual workVerbalising thinking; Self-monitoring; Concentration – resisting distraction or interruption; Seeking information and feedback; Gestures externalising thought process.
2. Group interaction without teacherGestures externalising thought process; Questioning; Completing peer utterances; Enhancing ideas; Giving directions, explanations or information; Justifying an argument.
3. Group interaction with teacherReflective self-questioning; Giving information; Explaining procedures and reasoning; Questions to teacher; Answering teacher's questions.
4. Whole class interactionQuestions to teacher; Answering teacher's questions; Making evaluative comments; Contributing ideas; Completing teacher's utterances.
